items.title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
items.raw_content: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. A key insight is that tasks with different modalities and surface forms can share the same underlying capability requirements. We therefore introduce The Trinity, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. Drawing on verified execution trajectories, Evolver shifts the basis of task organization from surface categories to shared requirements, reorganizing the original task tree into a hierarchical capability tree. We introduce Capability-Driven Real2Sim2Real: for heterogeneous t
items.title_zh: The Trinity：多模态智能体递归自我改进
items.summary: The Trinity is a recursive self-improvement framework for multimodal agents that couples world generation with harness evolution through Creator, Explorer and Evolver roles, reorganizing tasks by shared capability requirements.

items.title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.raw_content: Long-horizon LLM agents interact with their environments through complete assistant turns while generating each action token by token. We observe that critic values vary primarily across turns, motivating optimization anchored at turns with finer credit allocation among tokens. We propose Multiscale Policy Optimization (MPO), combining Multiscale Advantage Estimation (MAE) and turn-level importance sampling to align credit assignment and policy updates at the turn scale. Extensive experiments across search, tool-use, and automation tasks with 4B and 30B-A3B models demonstrate consistent gains over strong RL baselines.
items.title_zh: MPO：长程智能体的多尺度策略优化
items.summary: Multiscale Policy Optimization aligns credit assignment and policy updates at the turn level for long-horizon LLM agents, with gains over RL baselines on search, tool-use and automation tasks at 4B and 30B-A3B scale.

items.title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence
items.raw_content: Training a spatial VLM to answer which side an object lies on does not require it to preserve the metric displacement that determines that answer, while supervision for a distance estimate may leave categorical relations largely unconstrained. When post-training emphasizes one readout, improvements can therefore concentrate on that interface while transfer to others remains weak or even degrades; we call this observed specialization interface lock-in. ChronoReplay addresses it by replaying heterogeneous spatial supervision as chronologically ordered episodes, retaining source-native targets, and balancing supervision across families. Under the same observation access, a single ChronoReplay checkpoint improves OVO-S-Bench, OST-Bench, and UCS-Bench together, including a 13.41-point gain on OST-Bench, and achieves the highest three-benchmark mean among the supervision settings compared here
items.title_zh: ChronoReplay：打破空间智能的接口锁定
items.summary: ChronoReplay tackles interface lock-in in spatial VLMs by replaying mixed spatial supervision as episodes ordered in time with source-native targets, improving OVO-S-Bench, OST-Bench and UCS-Bench together.

items.title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
items.raw_content: Discrete visual tokens represent vision in a discrete form analogous to language, offering a native interface for multimodal modeling under a shared next-token prediction objective. However, quantization error is widely assumed to cause unavoidable semantic loss, fundamentally limiting the semantic fidelity of discrete visual tokens and positioning continuous visual representations as an intrinsic upper bound. Using multimodal understanding as a proxy for semantic fidelity, we revisit this assumption and find quantization error unreliable, as discrete representations with substantially larger errors can achieve better understanding. Instead, the effective bit budget of discrete indices emerges as a key determinant of downstream performance. items.title_zh: 离散视觉 token 是否语义无损？
items.summary: The paper challenges the assumption that quantization error makes discrete visual tokens semantically lossy, finding that effective bit budget better predicts downstream multimodal understanding than error alone.

items.title: HABIT-Bench: Evaluating Habit Induction from Longitudinal Weak Evidence in Agent Memory
items.raw_content: In long-term interactions with large language model (LLM) agents, users reveal habits through their choices and actions. These habits capture implicit user information that agents must infer across conversations. However, individual observations may provide only partial evidence about a habit or when it applies. Retaining past interactions alone does not ensure that agents can infer habits and apply them appropriately. We introduce HABIT-Bench to evaluate how well agent memory systems infer habits from weak evidence and apply them to later requests. We construct synthetic user histories from task-oriented dialogue data and controlled habit graphs. The histories span hundreds of sessions across food, finance, software, and travel. Four-choice tasks assess agents' ability to infer user habits and apply them appropriately. They include temporary exceptions, changes in habits, and suggestion
items.title_zh: HABIT-Bench：从弱证据推断用户习惯
items.summary: HABIT-Bench evaluates whether agent memory systems can infer user habits from partial, longitudinal evidence and apply them to later requests, using synthetic histories spanning hundreds of sessions.

items.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
items.raw_content: Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explore counterfactual futures. We introduce Rollback, a policy improvement paradigm that turns world models from passive simulators into counterfactual engines: it rolls back to critical decision points, branches into alternative actions, and contrasts their outcomes to attribute success to individual decisions. This concentrates imagination where it matters most and distills counterfactual outcomes into fine-grained, action-level supervision without a separately learned value model. items.title_zh: Rollback：在世界模型中回滚经验
items.summary: Rollback turns action-conditioned world models into counterfactual engines that rewind to critical decision points, branch into alternative actions and distill the outcomes into action-level supervision for robot policies.
